q: A topological dynamical system (X,T) is topologically mixing if for any two nonempty open sets U, V:
opts: There exists N such that Tⁿ(U) ∩ V ≠ ∅ for all n ≥ N
The orbit of every point is dense
exp: Topological mixing: eventually, every pair of open sets U, V has Tⁿ(U)∩V ≠ ∅ for all large n (not just some n, as in transitivity). Mixing implies transitivity; Bernoulli shifts are mixing but irrational rotations are transitive but not mixing.
